sections.h2: Where is West Hartford, and how big is the town?
sections.html:
West Hartford is a town in Hartford County, about 5 miles west of downtown Hartford, in the Capitol Planning Region.

It covers about 22 square miles and had 64,083 residents at the 2020 Census. It borders Hartford, Bloomfield, Newington, New Britain, Farmington and Avon. The land climbs from around 120 feet at Town Hall to 778 feet on Talcott Mountain, part of the Metacomet Ridge, where the Metropolitan District keeps reservoirs.

The median age was 41.5 in the 2010 Census, with 17.1% of residents 65 or older and 29.1% of households made up of one person living alone. Older owners downsizing or heirs settling an estate are common sellers in a town with that profile.

The town runs under a council-manager system, which it has used since 1919. As in the rest of Connecticut there is no county government, so the town handles assessment, building and recording.

sections.h2: What are the main areas of West Hartford?
sections.html:
West Hartford Center is the best known area, centered on Farmington Avenue and North and South Main Street.

The Center has been the commercial hub since the late 1600s, and Blue Back Square, opened in 2007, added retail, offices and apartments there. Other parts of town have their own character.

  • West Hartford Center and Blue Back Square, near Farmington Avenue.
  • Elmwood in the southeast, once the home of clay and pottery works and later factories.
  • Bishops Corner, which opened as a retail center in 1971.
  • West Hill, a planned 1920s neighborhood of Colonial Revival and Tudor Revival homes that became a National Historic District in 1996.
  • The Prospect Avenue and Elizabeth Park side of town, which has some National Register homes.

Interstate 84 was finished in 1969 and cut through the town, separating Elmwood from the rest. A seller's street can feel like a different market depending on which side of the highway it sits.

sections.h2: What is West Hartford's history, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
West Hartford began as the West Division of Hartford in 1672 and became its own town on May 3, 1854.

The town grew with the trolley and then the car. Between 1910 and 1930 the population jumped from 4,808 to 24,941, and by 1960 it reached 62,382. The town built a new elementary school every year in the 1950s to keep up.

In 1924 West Hartford became the first Connecticut municipality to adopt zoning. Its zoning has long kept multi-family housing separate from single-family neighborhoods, and Wikipedia notes that recent attempts to build multi-family housing have drawn resident protests. For a seller with a two-family house or a lot with an extra unit, check the current zoning before assuming what a buyer can do with the property.

Large colonials, ranches and split levels from the 1950s through 1970s fill the northern, western and far southwestern parts of town. Those houses are now 50 to 70 years old, so kitchens, baths and mechanical systems are common repair items.

sections.h2: Who employs people in West Hartford?
sections.html:
The Town of West Hartford and the University of Hartford are the two largest employers, each listed at 1,100 to 2,250 employees in the town's 2025 annual financial report.

Pratt and Whitney Measurement Systems once employed over 7,000 people at a plant here at its World War II peak, and the plant stood until 1991. Westfarms Mall opened in 1974 on the southwest edge of town and has more than 1.3 million square feet of stores and restaurants. The University of Saint Joseph is the other campus in town, next to the University of Hartford.

sections.h2: How do roads, buses and schools work in West Hartford?
sections.html:
Interstate 84 runs through the town, and CTfastrak bus rapid transit connects it to Hartford and New Britain.

CTfastrak opened in 2015, and West Hartford has two stations, Elmwood at New Park and New Britain Avenues and Flatbush Avenue at New Park Avenue. CT Transit runs routes along Albany Avenue, New Britain Avenue, Park Street, Main Street, Farmington Avenue, Asylum Avenue, Hillside Avenue and South Quaker Lane. A Hartford Line rail stop at Flatbush Avenue has been planned, but Wikipedia reports funding is not in place.

West Hartford Public Schools has two high schools, Conard and Hall, three middle schools (King Philip, Sedgwick and Bristow) and 11 elementary schools. Utilities are Eversource for electric, the Metropolitan District for water and Connecticut Natural Gas.

sections.h2: What taxes and paperwork apply when you sell in West Hartford?
sections.html:
The seller, or the seller's attorney, files Connecticut Form OP-236 for the conveyance tax when the deed is recorded with the West Hartford town clerk.

The Department of Revenue Services says the tax is due on transfers of $2,000 or more unless an exemption applies, and West Hartford's town code on the form is 155. The town's tax office says real estate bills for the 2025 Grand List are due July 1, 2026 and January 1, 2027. A sale that closes between those dates usually means the unpaid portion gets settled at closing, so ask the tax office for a current balance.

  • Check the tax office for any delinquent ordinance violation notices tied to the property.
  • Ask whether a bank escrow account is paying your bills.
  • Look at the town's revaluation page to see how a new assessment may affect the next bill.

We could not open the town's assessor page, so we have left out the revaluation year and the current mill rate. The tax office can confirm both.

sections.h2: What do West Hartford sellers often face, and how does a cash sale fit?
sections.html:
Many West Hartford owners list with an agent, and some choose a quicker private sale when the house needs work or time is short.

  • Houses from the 1950s through 1970s that need updating before a typical buyer's lender will approve them.
  • Inherited homes where family members live out of state.
  • Rental properties with tenants who are not leaving soon.
  • Owners who must move on a date set by a job, a divorce or an assisted living placement.

The town's median household income was reported at $99,280 in 2018, and the town's own housing stock ranges from historic districts to postwar subdivisions. A cash offer removes the lender's appraisal and inspection requirements from the process. Whether it is the right route depends on the house, your timeline and what a listing would net after commission and repairs.

If you are weighing the options, send us the address and the condition of the house. We will tell you what we can offer, and you can compare it against a listing at your own pace.

faqs.q: What county is West Hartford in?
faqs.a: West Hartford is in Hartford County, in the Capitol Planning Region. Connecticut abolished county government, so the town clerk, not a county office, records your deed.

faqs.q: When are West Hartford property taxes due?
faqs.a: The town tax office lists real estate bills for the 2025 Grand List as due July 1, 2026 and January 1, 2027. Confirm your exact balance with the tax office before closing.
The 2020 Census counted 64,083 residents in West Hartford. The town covers about 22 square miles.

faqs.q: Is there a conveyance tax when I sell a West Hartford house?
faqs.a: Yes, unless an exemption applies. The state requires Form OP-236 when the price is $2,000 or more, and West Hartford's town code on the form is 155.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Hartford house with tenants or violations?
faqs.a: Yes, you can sell it as it stands. Ask the tax office about any delinquent ordinance violation notices, and tell any buyer, including us, about tenants and open issues up front.
